docs.task: How the repo brief is built and capped: its character limit, where it is truncated, the note it adds, and its tests.

asks: How the repo brief is built
The note it adds when truncated

data_flow.step: AgentsFactory::build renders the spawn block, gathers the workspace instructions, ArtifactsBrief::read(ws), and BooksBrief::read(ws), then calls augment(&block, &BriefInput{...}). profile, inventory and project_docs come from the spawn environment (env.profile, env.inventory, env.project_docs). project_docs was read earlier by brief::project_docs in runner.rs.

augment returns the message unchanged if it already contains any of the five brief headings (BRIEF_HEADING, PROJECT_DOCS_HEADING, ARTIFACTS_HEADING, BOOKS_HEADING, INSTRUCTIONS_HEADING). Otherwise it calls build_brief and joins the result with the trimmed first message using a blank line, '---', and a blank line.

build_brief selects sections for the agent via sections(agent). Initializer gets none. Only when a profile exists and the agent has sections does it build the body: Stack, Commands, Testing, Skills (max 16 rows), Conventions, Review, Modules (max 10 rows, only when the prompt names paths). Values the inventory text already states are skipped via stated_in; individual values are shortened by truncate.

If the body is non-empty, the profile block is formatted as the heading '## Repo brief for <agent>', an intro sentence, the joined body sections, and a closing sentence naming the INVENTORY.md path. This is the only string subject to MAX_BRIEF_CHARS. If its char count is over 3600, it is cut to 3600 chars and '\n(brief truncated; see the inventory for the rest)' is appended.

Later blocks are appended in this order and are not subject to the 3600 cap: Project instructions (each file capped at 12000 chars, own note), Projects created in this session, Workspace artifacts (max 40 entries from ostra_core::artifacts::MAX_BRIEF_ARTIFACTS), Workspace documentation (max 20 books), Workspace instructions. The blocks are joined by blank lines. None is returned if there are no blocks.

patterns.description: The profile-derived block is assembled as one string (heading, intro sentence, body sections, closing inventory pointer). If its char count exceeds MAX_BRIEF_CHARS it is cut to exactly MAX_BRIEF_CHARS chars and the note is appended after the cut. The cut is on char boundaries (chars().take), not on a line or section boundary, so it can end mid-row, and the closing 'full inventory is at ...' sentence is the part most likely to be lost. The note is 49 characters plus a leading newline, so a truncated block is 3650 characters long, which is above the constant.
patterns.name: Cap the profile block by characters, then append a note outside the cap

patterns.description: Each project instruction file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, AGENT.md) is capped separately at MAX_PROJECT_DOC_CHARS = 12000 chars, then a different note is appended, preceded by a blank line. These files are not subject to MAX_BRIEF_CHARS because they are pushed as their own block after the profile block.
patterns.name: Per-file instruction cap with a different note

patterns.description: Individual profile values are squashed to single-line whitespace and shortened by truncate(value, limit), which keeps limit-1 chars and adds a single '…'. Limits in use: 48 (skill use-for), 150 (test matches), 190 (test note, naming, convention notes), 90 (test reports, immutability keyword), 170 (review rule). These keep rows small before the whole-block cap applies.
patterns.name: Per-field truncation with an ellipsis

patterns.description: Tests build a ProjectProfile with the profile() helper, build a BriefInput with every field set (agent, prompt, repo_root, profile, inventory, instructions, project_docs, artifacts, books, new_projects), call build_brief or augment, and assert with contains / starts_with. A struct-update (..input) switches the agent. A cap test would follow this shape with a profile or inventory large enough to pass 3600 chars.
patterns.name: Brief unit test shape

document.problem: The repo brief is appended to every execution's first message. A single constant, MAX_BRIEF_CHARS = 3600, caps only the profile-derived block, and one truncation site cuts it and appends a fixed note. No test exercises that cap or the note, and the docs page states the cap more broadly than the code applies it.

document.title: Repo brief construction and character cap

submit.findings_summary: The brief is built by build_brief in crates/ostra-agents/src/brief.rs and attached by augment, which AgentsFactory::build in ostra-engine calls. MAX_BRIEF_CHARS = 3600 caps only the profile block headed '## Repo brief for <agent>'. At brief.rs:409-412 an over-length block is cut to 3600 chars on a char boundary, and '\n(brief truncated; see the inventory for the rest)' is appended after the cut, so the block can be 3650 chars. Project instruction files have a separate 12000-char per-file cap with a different note, and artifacts, books and workspace instructions are not capped by characters. No test in crates/ostra-agents/src/tests.rs covers either cap or either note. The existing brief tests only cover section selection, idempotence and the block order. docs/internals/agents.md line 318 says 'The brief is limited to 3,600 characters', which is broader than the code.
